answer: In-person meetup verification makes each identity cost a real body. To register, an account attends a gathering where members from different lineages cross-check it face to face and co-sign an on-chain attestation. Like light through a prism, each applicant is examined from several angles - interview, document check, peer questioning - so one operator cannot hide behind many masks. Attestations are staked: if a fake cluster is unmasked at the next summit review, every co-signer is slashed. Each fake identity needs a separate human at a table, and one marble of forgery burns the group's bonds.
